page: Microsoft Azure D96als_v7 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine from the Dalsv7 series running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector operations and cryptographic extensions.

The instance includes 192 GB of system memory, providing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for compute-heavy applications rather than memory-heavy systems. It does not provide bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the D96als_v7 achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core processing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and bzip3 decompression, alongside top-tier large block memory write throughput of 172.54 GB/sec.

By provisioning a compact 2 GB RAM per core allocation, the hardware profile prioritizes dense compute capabilities over expansive memory capacity, offering cost-efficient compute scaling for CPU-bound tasks. Tradeoffs include reliance on external storage arrays and the absence of discrete GPU acceleration. The D96als_v7 is suitable for high-concurrency batch processing, compression routines, CPU-based machine learning inference, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and microservices workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D96als_v7 is a compute-focused instance within the Dalsv7 series, powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, supported by AVX-512 instruction extensions. The configuration allocates 192 GB of system RAM, yielding a 2 GB per vCPU ratio that prioritizes raw compute density over memory scale. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Benchmark data confirms top-tier multi-core computing, fast cryptographic processing, and strong memory bandwidth, including 172.54 GB/sec large-block write throughput and high Redis operation throughput. Given its reduced memory footprint per core, this instance offers an efficient compute-to-resource tradeoff for high-throughput batch computation, large-scale software compilation, CPU-driven inference tasks, and distributed web serving.
